Question B-003-013-001.

Why the correct answer is right: FM receivers have very high gain before the discriminator, so with no carrier to quiet the receiver the noise becomes loud.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "The very large gain of stages ahead of the discriminator": This is the correct choice because FM receivers have very high gain before the discriminator, so with no carrier to quiet the receiver the noise becomes loud.
- sourceIndex 1: "The additional gain following the discriminator": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from The very large gain of stages ahead of the discriminator. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "The nature of atmospheric noise in the VHF range": This answer would fit a different fault than The very large gain of stages ahead of the discriminator. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, noise control may be useful elsewhere, but this choice points to the wrong block or symptom.
- sourceIndex 3: "The higher intermediate frequency used in FM receivers": This option confuses another station topic with The very large gain of stages ahead of the discriminator. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, more of that quantity would not address the fault and can make a clean-signal problem worse.
